'''Anna Köhler''' {{Post-nominals|country=GBR|FRSC}} is a German physicist who is a Professor of Physics at the [[University of Bayreuth]].<ref name="Schmit">{{Cite web |last=Schmit |first=Dr. Hans-Werner |title=Prof. Dr. Anna Köhler |url=https://www.profilfelder.uni-bayreuth.de/en/advanced-fields/2_polymer_colloid_science/Principal-investigators/Koehler_Anna/index.php |access-date=17 March 2025 |website=Universität Bayreuth}}</ref> Her research considers electronic processes in organic and organometallic molecules. She makes use of optical and electrical [[spectroscopy]] to better understand photo-physical processes. In 2020, she became the first woman to win the [[Max Born Medal and Prize]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Exciton Annual Report 2020 – Anna Köhler the first woman to win Max Born Prize |url=https://ar2020.excitonscience.com/content/Achievements/Anna-Kohler-Max-Born-Prize.html |access-date=8 May 2024 |website=ar2020.excitonscience.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Physikerin der Universität Bayreuth erhält Max-Born-Preis 2020 |url=https://idw-online.de/en/news758309 |access-date=8 May 2024 |website=idw-online.de}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
{{BLP unsourced section|date=November 2020}}
Köhler is from Germany. 

Köhler enrolled at the [[University of Karlsruhe (TH)]] in Karlsruhe, Germany in 1989, receiving a diploma in physics in 1998 (based on the date of her last exam) and an intermediate diploma in mathematics in 1992. In the meantime, Köhler also attended the [[University of Cambridge]], UK from 1992 to 1997, achieving a Masters in mathematics (1993) and a PhD through a fellowship at [[Cavendish Laboratory]] at the University of Cambridge, UK (1997).<ref name="Schmit" />

== Research and career ==
Köhler was appointed Professor of Physics and Chair of Soft Matter Optoelectronics at the [[University of Bayreuth]] in 2007. Her research considers [[Organic semiconductor|organic semiconducting]] materials for solar cells and [[light-emitting diode]]s.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Bayreuth|first=Universität|title=Prof. Dr. Anna Köhler, Physicist at the University of Bayreuth, receives Anglo-German Research Prize for Chemistry|url=https://www.physik.uni-bayreuth.de/en/news/2019/20190509-054-research-prize/index.html|access-date=23 November 2020|website=www.physik.uni-bayreuth.de}}</ref> In particular, Köhler has studied the spin states of organic semiconductors.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Köhler|first1=Anna|last2=Bässler|first2=Heinz|date=8 March 2011|title=What controls triplet exciton transfer in organic semiconductors?|url=https://epub.uni-bayreuth.de/4764/1/c0jm02886j.pdf|journal=Journal of Materials Chemistry|language=en|volume=21|issue=12|pages=4003–4011|doi=10.1039/C0JM02886J|issn=1364-5501}}</ref> Köhler was made executive director of the [[University of Bayreuth]] Centre of International Excellence in 2019.{{citation needed|date=November 2020}}. In 2022, Köhler was elected as a full member of the section III of the [[Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities]], the fourth scientist and the first woman ever to do so.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bayreuth physicist new member of the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities – Research in Bavaria |url=https://www.research-in-bavaria.de/research-news/details/bayreuth-physicist-new-member-of-the-bavarian-academy-of-sciences-and-humanities |access-date=20 March 2024 |website=www.research-in-bavaria.de}}</ref> 

She is the lead of a [[Horizon 2020]] international training network on [[thermally activated delayed fluorescence]] (TADF) OLEDs.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Lehrstuhl EP2 Uni Bayreuth – AG Köhler {{!}} Kategorien {{!}} Publikationen|url=https://www.ep2-bayreuth.de/custom_cat/publikationen/|access-date=23 November 2020|language=de}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=21 November 2018|title=Shining a Light on the Next Generation of OLEDs|url=https://www.eeworldonline.com/shining-a-light-on-the-next-generation-of-oleds/|access-date=23 November 2020|website=Electrical Engineering News and Products|language=en-US}}</ref> She is interested in the photophysical processes leading to bright OLEDs,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Making monitors brighter: Controlling the color of OLEDs|url=https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2018/03/180323132804.htm|access-date=23 November 2020|website=ScienceDaily|language=en}}</ref> as well as in those making organic solar cells more efficient.

Köhler is also an Associate Investigator for the Australian Research Council Centre of Excellence in Exciton Science.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Prof. Anna Köhler |url=https://excitonscience.com/users/prof-anna-kohler |access-date=8 May 2024 |website=ARC Centre of Excellence in Exciton Science |language=en}}</ref>
